learning_objective: 🎯 Discover who really runs the government! Learn about the President, the Prime Minister, and the massive civil service that implements laws.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The branch of government responsible for implementing laws and policies. It includes the political executive (ministers) and the permanent executive (civil servants/bureaucracy).

In a Presidential system (like the USA), the President is the real head of government. In India's Parliamentary system, the President is the nominal (ceremonial) head, while the real power lies with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.

Elected indirectly. Acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers. The President has specific 'discretionary powers', such as sending back a bill for reconsideration or choosing a PM when no party has a clear majority.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🎙️ The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
main_concepts.simple_explanation: The PM is the head of the government. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. If they lose the confidence of the Lok Sabha, they must resign.
Trained and skilled officers (like IAS, IPS) who remain in office even when the ruling party changes. They assist ministers in formulating policies and implementing them on the ground.

fun_activity.title: 👑 Who is the Real Boss?
fun_activity.instructions: Think of the President as the 'Grandparent' of a family (gets respect, gives advice, signs the final papers) and the Prime Minister as the 'Parent' (makes the daily decisions and runs the house). This is the Parliamentary system!

exam_tips: 📌 Always use the phrase 'collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha' when discussing the Council of Ministers.
📌 List the 3 specific situations where the President exercises discretionary power.
📌 Differentiate between the Political Executive (elected, temporary) and the Permanent Executive (selected, permanent).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Vice President acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
⭐ An amendment limits the size of the Council of Ministers to 15% of the total members of the Lok Sabha.
⭐ The civil service provides stability and continuity to administration.
